title: Security & Compliance Review - Pen Test & Vulnerability Management
summary: Review of latest pen test results and Redwood’s vulnerability management / secure SDLC practices. Discussed critical/ high findings, remediation timelines, patch cadence, KMS/encryption, RBAC/SSO, and next steps for evidence share and follow-up benchmark. Agreed to share pen test report and schedule a technical deep dive with infra team.
transcript:
Header: 2025-07-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Alex, Sofia, Priya (Redwood); Jordan, Maya, Devon, Riley (Acme Health)

[00:00] Alex Reed: Hey everyone thanks for joining we have about 40 minutes, quick intros, and we'll dig into the pen test and follow-ups.
[00:12] Jordan Blake: Thanks Alex, yeah Maya and I are here, Devon and Riley as well, excited to get into the details.
[00:20] Sofia Martinez: Hi all, Sofia from Redwood, I focus on infra and sec integrations, Priya's on for deeper vuln questions.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Great, we want to focus on the critical/high items and your patch cadence and how you track remediation. Also KMS scope and retention of audit logs.
[00:40] Alex Reed: Perfect thanks, quick agenda, we'll run through the pen test summary, then vuln mgmt process, SDLC controls, and finish with action items.
[01:05] Sofia Martinez: Quick housekeeping, the pen test referenced here is the June engagement with external red team partner, scope included hosted API and dedicated nodes. Some findings were surface-level config, others were code-level dependency issues.
[01:28] Maya Patel: Right, question - is that pen test report the full report or an exec summary? We only saw the summary in the portal.
[01:35] Alex Reed: We will share the full report under NDA, the portal summary is intentionally high level. Full report will include PoCs and remediation notes.
[01:45] Devon Liu: Did you find any RCE or auth bypasses? Those are our big concerns with ePHI scope.
[01:52] Priya Nair: No unauth RCEs in scope, the highest severity were privilege escalation from misconfigured role mapping on a legacy admin endpoint and a few dependency CVEs with high CVSS. Some timing issues around token expiration were flagged but mitigations were in place.
[02:15] Jordan Blake: Ok that's helpful, can you share CVE ids so we can cross-reference with our vulnerability scanners?
[02:22] Sofia Martinez: Yes we'll include the CVE list and patch status per item. We track each finding in our vuln tracker, assign severity, and map to remediation SLAs.
[02:36] Riley Carter: What's your SLA for critical vs high? We need to align with our contract expectations.
[02:42] Alex Reed: Our internal target is 72 hours for critical remediation triage and a remediation plan within 7 days; high is typically 14 days for plan and patching cadence depends on complexity. We can commit to contract-level wording for Dedicated/Private with agreed SLAs.
[03:05] Maya Patel: Can you describe the process end-to-end? From discovery to patch to verification and evidence?
[03:12] Priya Nair: Sure, triage into our tracker, assign owner, create a remediation branch if code-level, schedule patch window for infra, run dependency updates and tests, then a verification run by QA and security, close with evidence (PRs, ops runbooks, screenshots of scans). We also attach CVE references and mitigation notes.
[03:36] Jordan Blake: How do you handle vendor/third-party dependencies that require upstream fixes?
[03:42] Sofia Martinez: If upstream is required, we apply temporary mitigations (disable feature, isolate service, add WAF rule) and track upstream PRs. We also have compensating controls and a documented escalation to engineering leadership.
[04:00] Devon Liu: Patch cadence — what's the typical kernel/OS and container image update schedule for dedicated/private nodes?
[04:08] Priya Nair: For hosted we push patches weekly for critical OS packages, and monthly for regular updates. Dedicated/private customers can opt into automated monthly patching or a quarterly schedule; emergency patches are pushed immediately with coordinated maintenance windows.
[04:30] Maya Patel: For our environment we need at-most-two-week turnaround on critical patches. Can that be guaranteed for Private?
[04:36] Alex Reed: For Private with SLA we can lock in a 14-day critical remediation commitment and provide evidence. We'll need to put that in the SOW.
[04:48] Riley Carter: Ok good. Next, KMS/encryption scope: do you encrypt data at rest by default? How is customer key separation handled?
[04:58] Sofia Martinez: Data at rest is encrypted by default. For hosted we manage keys via our KMS, keys are tenant-scoped. For Private we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) and HSM integration. We log key usage in audit logs with key IDs.
[05:18] Maya Patel: Audit logs retention — we need 1 year immutable logs for compliance. Can you provide that?
[05:24] Priya Nair: Audit logs are configurable; for enterprise customers we can set retention to 12 months and export to the customer's SIEM via secure transfer. Immutable retention (WORM) is supported for Private deployments.
[05:40] Jordan Blake: What about RBAC and SSO? We need SCIM provisioning and role-based restrictions so only certain roles can export raw transcripts.
[05:48] Sofia Martinez: We support SAML SSO, OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. We have built-in roles and the ability to create custom roles and restrict actions like export, admin, and billing. SCIM sync interval is configurable.
[06:10] Maya Patel: How do you validate config drift and ensure RBAC rules aren't changed without proper approvals?
[06:16] Priya Nair: We keep infra-as-code for roles and maintain a change log; changes go through PRs and require two approvers for sensitive role changes. Drift detection runs nightly and alerts to the security channel.
[06:34] Alex Reed: Quick pause - any other compliance artifacts you need? SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert status?
[06:42] Jordan Blake: Yes, we need evidence of SOC 2 Type II and your latest iso audit scope.
[06:47] Sofia Martinez: We are SOC 2 Type II certified; the latest report and bridge letter can be shared under NDA. We are in progress with ISO 27001 and will share the scope doc.
[06:58] Riley Carter: Back to pen test, are vulnerabilities triaged by both severity and exploitability?
[07:03] Priya Nair: Yes we score by CVSS and an internal exploitability index that considers access required, PoC complexity, and impact to ePHI. PoCs are flagged and assigned higher priority.
[07:20] Jordan Blake: For the dependency CVEs, do you use automated SCA (software composition analysis)? Which tool?
[07:26] Sofia Martinez: We use a combination of SCA tools (OSS scanning and an internal aggregator); I won't call out vendor names on-call but we can include tooling list in the artifact. We have CI gates to block builds with certain severities.
[07:40] Maya Patel: Do you require security sign-off per release? We need to ensure nothing gets out without review.
[07:46] Priya Nair: Yes security gate in CI for critical and high SCA results; releases require security approver for changes that touch sensitive scopes. Low-risk changes can be auto-approved after tests.
[08:02] Devon Liu: How do you handle emergency hotfixes that bypass normal CI gating?
[08:08] Alex Reed: Emergency process includes a documented hotfix runbook, mandatory post-mortem, and a retroactive security review; we escalate and backfill tests.
[08:18] Jordan Blake: Are there automated canary rollouts to limit blast radius?
[08:22] Sofia Martinez: Yes our deployment pipeline supports progressive rollouts and canary traffic shifting; we also have circuit breakers and automatic rollback on error/anomaly thresholds.
[08:33] Maya Patel: Let's talk about proof-of-remediation. After you patch, can you run the same external tests and provide scan outputs?
[08:40] Priya Nair: Yes we coordinate re-tests with the red team or run internal verification scans and provide artifacts (scan reports, PR links, screenshots). For critical issues we recommend a retest by an external pen test partner.
[08:56] Riley Carter: Good. Another question - do you have an SLA for time-to-evidence for audit requests?
[09:02] Alex Reed: For enterprise we commit to a 5-business-day evidence delivery window for SOC/Security artifact requests; we can shorten if part of contract.
[09:12] Maya Patel: Can we get a dedicated security contact for escalations?
[09:16] Alex Reed: Yes we'll assign a named CSM/Technical contact; Priya will be the escalation owner for vuln matters initially.
[09:24] Sofia Martinez: Quick note, sometimes transcription in your portal scrambles product names, sorry if you saw Redwood product names wrong, e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" might appear as "Redwood dedicate" in the transcript exports.
[09:40] Jordan Blake: Noted, thanks.
[09:45] Alex Reed: Moving on to secure SDLC: we use static analysis + SCA + pre-merge tests. We also have threat modeling for new features and monthly security reviews.
[10:00] Maya Patel: Is threat modeling mandatory for anything that touches ePHI?
[10:04] Priya Nair: Yes, any feature touching ePHI requires threat modeling and an approval flow. We document mitigations in the ticket.
[10:15] Devon Liu: What about dependency update cadence and automated PRs?
[10:20] Sofia Martinez: We run daily dependency checks and auto-open PRs for non-breaking updates; critical CVEs trigger an immediate alert and auto-PR with higher priority.
[10:35] Jordan Blake: For node images, are you using signed images and image provenance?
[10:40] Priya Nair: Yes images are signed and we track SBOMs for each image; provenance is logged and available in the console for each deployment.
[11:00] Riley Carter: Regarding pen test notes, one of our auditors asked about your patching deployment windows, downtime expectations.
[11:06] Alex Reed: Most patches are zero-downtime with rolling restarts; for kernel-level changes there may be short maintenance windows, we communicate in advance and offer off-hours scheduling.
[11:22] Maya Patel: Do you notify customers about CVEs that affect them specifically?
[11:26] Sofia Martinez: Yes we have an incident communication process that notifies affected customers with severity, impact, and recommended actions.
[11:36] Jordan Blake: Any open items from the June pen test we should be aware of today?
[11:42] Priya Nair: There were three open high items: one dependency CVE (tracked and PR open), one role-mapping config (patch deployed and awaiting verification), and a logging misconfiguration (remediated). Two of them are in verification stage.
[12:00] Riley Carter: Can you share the tracker IDs so our team can follow status?
[12:05] Sofia Martinez: Yes we will share tracker links and the mapping table.
[12:12] Alex Reed: Ok going to speed through remaining items... audit log exports, retention configuration, and evidence with time stamps.
[12:24] Maya Patel: For export controls, we want an approval step before anyone can export raw transcripts.
[12:30] Priya Nair: We can attach a required approval flow and tie export permission to a role and an approval ticket in your ticketing system.
[12:45] Jordan Blake: Do you support data residency restrictions per region? We need EU-only processing for certain customers.
[12:51] Sofia Martinez: Yes we route requests to region-specific clusters and ensure data residency via deployment options; Private gives you full control.
[13:04] Devon Liu: How do you ensure your supply chain (third-party libs) isn't introducing malicious packages?
[13:10] Priya Nair: We do provenance checks, lockfiles, internal allowlists for critical packages, and periodic SCA + integrity verification. Suspicious packages are quarantined.
[13:28] Riley Carter: Do you rotate keys and what's your KMS rotation policy?
[13:32] Sofia Martinez: Key rotation is supported; default rotation is annually but customers can set more frequent rotations. For BYOK customers rotation policy is managed by their KMS.
[13:46] Maya Patel: Any known residual risk or caveats we should plan for?
[13:50] Priya Nair: The main residual risk is configuration drift in private deployments if customers manage infra; we mitigate with drift detection and periodic audits. For hosted, residual risk is typical cloud provider risk which we mitigate via defenses-in-depth.
[14:04] Jordan Blake: Ok makes sense. A couple administrative items: evidence zip, pen test full report, SLA wording, and a follow-up deep dive.
[14:12] Alex Reed: Next steps we'll capture those. Anything else from the customer team?
[14:18] Maya Patel: Can you include a list of the scanning tools and versions used in the report? We need that for our auditor.
[14:24] Sofia Martinez: Yes we'll include tool list, versions, and scan config.
[14:30] Devon Liu: Also, can we get a short runbook for emergency patching?
[14:34] Priya Nair: We'll share the hotfix runbook and contact list.
[14:40] Riley Carter: Great.
[14:45] Alex Reed: Recap of next steps and action items, then we'll close.
[15:00] Sofia Martinez: Action item list coming up.
[15:02] Alex Reed: Thanks everyone.

[End of transcript - timestamps approximate, transcription may include minor errors and misheard product names]
next_steps: Share full pen test report under NDA (Redwood)
Provide tracker links and CVE list (Redwood)
Send SLA wording for 14-day critical remediation for Private (Redwood legal)
Schedule a technical deep dive with Acme infra team (Redwood SE + Acme)
